scope: Request size/concurrency bounds, malformed JSON, connection lifecycle, resource exhaustion and error status semantics

findings.title: Request idle timeout (60s) is shorter than the composed control-operation bound (up to ~150s)
findings.evidence: idleTimeout: 60 on the API listener, while quiesce (src/coordinator.ts:725-745) chains up to four calls each bounded by SWARMFORGE_API_TIMEOUT_MS (30000) and cancel of a paused worker adds resumeWorker. Reproduced: cancel_worker returned only after 60021ms with a hanging fake provider (probe cancel.ts); isolated mechanism confirmed with Bun.serve idleTimeout 3 vs a 12s handler failing the client at 4002ms (probe idle2.ts).
findings.reproduction: /tmp/probe/cancel.ts (in-flight control call at the idleTimeout boundary), /tmp/probe/idle.ts, /tmp/probe/idle2.ts
findings.recommendation: Derive the idle timeout from the composed per-request budget (e.g. SWARMFORGE_API_TIMEOUT_MS * 5 + margin) or bound each mutating tool call as a whole so no request can exceed the connection budget.
findings.confidence: medium; deepest chained case (cancel3.ts) was cut off by the review deadline, so the worst-case figure is code-derived rather than measured

findings.title: /metrics render is unbounded per scrape and the metrics listener skips the host allowlist and bearer check
findings.evidence: Metrics listener (serve.ts:177-190) has no bearer/host check unlike http.ts:9-29. Metrics.render (metrics.ts:74-131) issues per-worker and per-dispatch SQL. Measured: 50ms at 200 retained workers, 731ms at 1000, 5125ms at 3000; store.all() alone 192ms at 3000.
findings.recommendation: Cache or pre-aggregate metrics instead of re-deriving from SQLite per scrape, apply the same bearer/host check to the metrics listener, and guard scrape concurrency.

findings.title: /events per-request cost scales with total retained workers via the redaction secret set
findings.evidence: redactorFor (security.ts:43-50) reads c.store.all() and appends one server_password per retained worker; text() (security.ts:5-23) scans every secret in raw, percent-encoded and base64 form. One /events replay of 100 events took 1981ms and 1986ms at 1000 retained workers; isolated text() cost 0.30ms at 10 rising to 9.11ms at 1000 retained.
findings.recommendation: Build the secret set once per response rather than per event and bound or index the per-worker secret contribution.

findings.title: No server-side concurrency cap; a single 123 KiB batched request registers 1000 store listeners
findings.evidence: maxRequestBodySize 131072 and the 413 check bound bytes, not calls. 1000 wait_for_state_change invocations fit in 123891 bytes and registered 1000 store listeners from one connection (pendingRequests 1). Each event then schedules a microtask fan-out; one event with 256 waiters cost 101ms synchronous, and 2000 waiters took 48s to settle. Bun's observed pendingRequests ceiling was 256, which is a transport limit, not an admission policy.
findings.recommendation: Cap concurrent in-flight requests and concurrent wait_for_state_change waiters explicitly with a 503/429 refusal, independent of request byte size.

findings.title: Transport-level throws collapse into a silent, undiagnosable 500
findings.evidence: The catch discards the error object and returns a bare 'MCP request failed' with no log line, no correlation id and no redacted detail. Genuine internal faults are indistinguishable in the field.
findings.recommendation: Log the redacted error before returning the 500; the redactor at security.ts is already available in this handler.

findings.title: Verified good: malformed JSON and oversize bodies are rejected correctly
findings.evidence: Empty body, bad JSON and a truncated object all return 400 Invalid JSON; null, 5, a JSON string and [1,2,3] return 400 with JSON-RPC -32700; declared-short content-length with a 200KB body and a chunked oversize body both return 413; a 298891-byte batch returns 413. No defect found in this area.
findings.recommendation: No change; recorded as scope coverage.

tests.result: 33 pass, 0 fail, 189 expect() calls, exit 0 (official Bun 1.4.2; snapshot Bun 1.3.14 cannot read lockfileVersion 2 and the lockfile was not rewritten)
tests.probes: 14 custom probes under /tmp/probe using fake providers only; 13 completed with exit 0, cancel3.ts cut off by the review deadline, cap.ts first run exceeded a shell timeout and was re-run smaller

limitations: One planned probe (cancel3.ts, 4x25s chained quiesce) was cut off by the 30-minute review deadline; F1's worst-case figure is code-derived, not measured
F2/F3/F4 costs are measured against synthetic retention on local SQLite with fake providers; real provider timings would differ but the unbounded-in-retained-rows shape is reproduced
Only 3 of 20 test files were run; the full suite is the whole-suite reviewer's scope
No real cloud, model provider or infrastructure smoke was performed and no credentials were used
Verdict is INCOMPLETE: findings stand on the evidence collected, but the scope was not exhausted within the budget
